JHA JHA Date:
NIRALA 2025.02.28 challenged the order dated 16.08.2023 (Annexure-A/1) passed 15:41:34 +0530 by the Appellate Tribunal / Sessions Judge Balod (C.G.), whereby it has dismissed the application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 along with appeal (unregistered) challenging the order dated 28.02.2023 (Annexure-A/2)
passed by the Additional District Magistrate and Adjudicating Officer, District Balod (C.G.), who has imposed the penalty against the appellants under Section 52(1), 55 &
58 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 (for short 'the Act of 2006').

Learned counsel for the appellants would submit that order passed by the Appellate Tribunal / Sessions Judge, is appealable before the High Court within 60 + 60 days under Section 71(6) of the Act of 2006.

He further submitted that due to inadvertence, impugned order passed by the Appellate Tribunal / Sessions Judge was challenged before the High Court by filing CRMP No.300/2024 on 16.01.2024, which was withdrawn on 13.01.2025 with liberty to file duly constituted appeal, as such,

sentences.text: after receiving certified copy of order dated 13.01.2025 by the appellants on 16.01.2025, instant miscellaneous appeal was filed immediately,
as such, after deducting the period wasted in filing the CRMP, instant appeal has been filed well within the period of limitation.
Hence, he prays that application for condonation of delay in filing miscellaneous appeal may be allowed.

Having considered the aforesaid facts and documents of the case, I.A. No.1/2025, application seeking condonation of delay in filing the miscellaneous appeal is allowed and the delay of 459 days'
in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.

Also heard on I.A. No.2/2025, application seeking leave of the Hon'ble High Court to implead Smt.
Minakshi Chandrakar, Food Safety Officer, Food and Drug Administration, District Balod (C.G.), as respondent in the miscellaneous appeal.

entities.text: Food and Drug Administration, District Balod
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Proposed Respondent Smt. Minakshi Chandrakar, Food Safety Officer had filed case in her official capacity, as such, she cannot be impleaded by her name / in-person, therefore, I.A, No.2/2025 is rejected and appellants are directed to delete the name of respondent No.1 from the cause title of memo of appeal.
Let necessary amendment be carried out to delete the name of respondent No.1 from the cause title of memo of appeal during the course of the day.
Also heard on I.A. No.4/2025, application seeking permission for amendment in the cause title of the miscellaneous appeal.
On due consideration and for the reasons mentioned in the application, I.A. No.4/2025 is allowed and appellants are permitted to implead State as party respondent No.3 in the cause title of memo of appeal.
Let necessary amendment be carried out in the cause title of memo of appeal to implead the State as respondent No.3 during the course of the day.
Mr. Rajeev Bharat, G.A. for the State is present before the Court, as such, his presence is marked for State/respondent No.3.
In view of above, remaining respondents be re-
numbered.

Also heard on I.A. No.3/2025,
application for grant of interim relief/stay.
State counsel seeks short time to file reply to I.A. No.3/2025.
Time is granted.

However, it is directed that effect and operation of the order dated 28.02.2023 (Annexure-A/2)
passed by the Additional District Magistrate and Adjudicating Officer, District Balod (C.G.) shall M/S. Hindustan Unilever Limited vs Narendra Kumar Jain on 28 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74932927/
2 remain stayed till the next date of hearing.
List the case on 4th March, 2025.
Sd/-
